author: Camemes
body:
Heyo,

This is a guide for new players to Avicus. There was an old post by {tag=739cef1a2e8b482da8442ebed62d8b4d} (https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/c3723efec) but that is 1 year old and hasn't been updated in a year.

So I will be covering basic topics such as navigating the server, forums, teamspeak and community slack, as well as some frequently asked questions that will be answered.

Let's do it!


REMEMBER: If you are unsure of ANYTHING, contact a staff member and they will happily answer your questions.



Rules:

The rules are important in-order to maintain a fun and friendly atmosphere.For a full list of rules, visit this website:https://avicus.net/rules/en.

Those who do not follow these rules will be punished in the form of a warn, kick, temporary ban or permanent ban. It is up to the staff member to determine which punishment best suits the situation. If you disagree with the punishment given to you, you may appeal it (refer to section on appealing infractions) and it may be removed if it is found to be false. It is up to the players to keep up with the rules, it is not staff responsibility if you re unaware of rule changes or additions. If you see rule breaks, please use /report (refer to section on reporting players for more info) rather than saying "HACKER" in chat. It makes our job as staff easier and so that the possibly hacker doesn't suspect us and toggle his/her hacks off making it harder for moderators.



Communication:

Want to get involved in the community? Well, Avicus provides a large amount of opportunities to interact and communicate.

In-game: Of course you can chat in game and /msg for private conversations.

Teamspeak 3: The Avicus Teamspeak server provides numerous channels you can join and voice chat with friends. You can also join the support channels for help from staff. It is the general platform we use for voice communication.

The Forums: Get involved in topics on the forums. Get to know the community and keep updated for new additions to the server and more!

Community Slack: Want an easy way to talk to the community? Fill this (http://goo.gl/forms/qeFOJVMqqn) form out or alternatively ask a slack admin (Resepignev, Piez or Jahaj) to invite your email, they'll send you an invite and help you join and get settled in. Refer to this post (https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/a9121e12c) for more information on rules, channels etc.



Appealing:

If you were banned or received an infraction and you believe the punishment is false or you feel you have been banned long enough, you can have the infraction removed by making an appeal here: (https://avicus.net/appeal) and explain why the punishment should be removed. The staff who punished you will respond to the appeal and if it was false, it will be removed. You can escalate the appeal to the senior staff team if you feel that you are being treated unfairly by the moderator dealing with your appeal, please note that escalated appeals take longer to deal with so bear that in mind when escalating. Please be patient and honest during your appeal. Lying and spamming will not help your chances. If you were banned however on teamspeak 3, you may appeal it under the sub-forum, Teamspeak Appeals/Reports (https://avicus.net/forums/categories/1508) Refer to {tag=3cce00809faa48f982cf64410305822a}'s guide for more information on appealing Teamspeak punishments.(https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/e0f2f1b36)



Reporting:

You have 2 options when it comes to reporting rules breakers:

/report [name] [reason] - this in-game command allows staff to deal with your report almost instantly. Do not spam this command as it may result in a punishment.

However, if no staff are online..

Get some evidence (video evidence preferred) of them breaking a rule and make a report on the forums under:https://avicus.net/forums/categories/47 where staff will handle reports and issue punishments.

Please do not spam /report. Please wait for your report to be dealt with and let the staff. A few factors that are involved in how quickly your report will be dealt with include:

  • The amount of players on: Chances are the more players on, the more reports coming through at one given time.

  • The amount of staff online: If there are only 1-2 staff members on, chances are your report will be dealt with later as they may have other reports to get through first.

  • What you reported them for/reason: If you report someone for aimbot and someone else reports for fly, most staff will handle the fly hacking report first as it is easier to ban off of. If you put more complex reasons, then your report will be filed after other reports are dealt with as they are take longer to finalise.

So please help the staff out by being a little patient and not spamming staff with reports.

Do not report staff on the forums or in-game! Report moderators and staff members abusing permissions or breaking the staff Code of Conduct (https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/8319110c3) with sufficient evidence and action will be taken against these staff by making a post here: (https://avicus.net/forums/categories/1509) or emailing support@avicus.net. If you wish to report players on Teamspeak, breaking our rules, you may do so under the sub-forum Teamspeak Appeals/Reports. (https://avicus.net/forums/categories/1508) Refer to {tag=38cc237d92724e01ad24f5b0110130c1}'s guide on reporting on teamspeak for more information: https://avicus.net/forums/discussions/f295e59ff.



Support:

If you need help from staff at all, you can email the support email at support@avicus.net or sales@avicus.net regarding purchase issues. You can also use the "Ask The Seniors" section on the forums: https://avicus.net/forums/categories/1504 If you want to verbally talk to someone, hop onto our Teamspeak 3 server (ts.avicus.net) join the support waiting room and wait for staff to help you out. For more help joining and downloading teamspeak, see https://avicus.net/teamspeak. Alternatively, check the Guides & Support sub-forum, that usually contains everything you need to know about the server and how it operates as well as ways to improve. (https://avicus.net/forums/categories/34)



Donating:

If you want a rank in-game and want to help the server out? Head to out shop: https://avicus.net/shop and buy 1 of our 3 donator ranks as well as exclusive badges, stat resets and keys to crates but we'll get to that later. With these ranks you can join full games, choose your team, multiply credits earned and get a cool prefix in-game, on teamspeak and the forums. You also gain a lot of cool new commands and features by donating such as access to /nh (name history) commands and more available badges to buy.



Staff applications:

Interested in applying for moderator or other staff positions? Keep updated on the forums and when staff applications open up, make a post here: https://avicus.net/forums/categories/1507 following the format and structure provided in a post by a senior staff member. Usually an Administrator will announce that apps have opened.

If your applications is decent, you may get accepted for an interview on Teamspeak.

If you pass your interview you will get a junior mod trial and training on what to do as a staff member.

However, this is only for the moderator position. Map Developer promotions are hand picked by the current map developers. Official positions are hand-picked, however, referee and media positions use applications which come out every-so-often when they are needed, most likely before a tournament.



Frequently Asked Questions:

Onto some frequently asked questions asked by new players.

Q: What are crates?

A: Crates are awarded at the end of a match to a random player. If you head over to our shop (https://avicus.net/shop) you can purchase keys to unlock the crates and unlock cool prizes and rewards. Also purchase donator ranks and you can purchase keys in-game with credits.

Q: What are credits? What are they used for?

A: Credits are our in-game currency. Earn credits by gaining kills and capturing objectives (destroying monuments, capturing wools etc.). If you go to the hub, you can use these credits to buy badges, sounds, trails and even gadgets in the hub, plus more!

Q: I need some help, but don’t know where to ask for it. Where do I ask for help?

A: You can ask staff in-game, on teamspeak or on the support email (support@avicus.net) or ask the community by making a new post under “Off Topic” (https://avicus.net/forums/categories/45) and wait for people to help you out as best they can.

Q: What’s a team and how do I join one?

A: A team are a group of players who compete in competitive scrimmages, official (or unofficial) tournaments and basically hang out with. If you want to join a team, either mate a “Looking For Team” post on the forums under the subtopic:https://avicus.net/forums/categories/48 or respond to another teams “Looking For Members” post under the suptopic:https://avicus.net/forums/categories/61 Or make your own team under https://avicus.net/teams/new.

Q: What do referee’s and officials do?

A: Officials create, manage and run tournaments whilst referee’s manage teams and make sure the tournament runs smoothly with no cheaters or problems. You can apply for referee positions when applications open, keep updated on the forums to know when applications open.

Q: What is a media? and how can I become one?

A: Media is a rank given to players who actively stream tournaments. You may apply when applications open, keep an eye out on the forums for that.

(Will update this section of the guide should new questions arise)



Map Creation

Interested in becoming a map maker and adding maps to rotations? Well, by making your original, non-plagiarized map, taking some screenshots, making an xml for it and submitting it under the forum subtopic: Map Releases (https://avicus.net/forums/categories/43) and perhaps you may see your map an everyday part of the rotations and player by the avicus community. To elaborate, create an original map with not only looks pleasing to the eye but also plays really well by other players. Now you need an xml done, you can either contact someone who knows how to do xml or look up tutorials on how to do it yourself. Don’t be afraid to do do something new and different, those are the maps that will be noticed by map developers. After that, you can submit your map with download and other players and map developers will leave comments on your map like what you did well and what you can improve on. Your map will then be given a final verdict and added to rotations if it is accepted. Don’t stress if your first map gets denied, on one can make a perfect map on their first go, it takes time. Keep trying though and you’ll get there eventually.



In-Game Commands:

There are some cool in-game commands that players may want to know.

/join - This puts you on a team and allows you to play in the match.

/leave - This puts you on the spectator team and takes you out of the match.

/t [message] - Team chat. Speak privately with your team.

/msg [player] [message] - Privately messages a player with a certain message.

/r [message] - Replies to someone who you messaged. Easier for back-and-forth messaging.

/report [player] [reason] - Report rule breakers to the staff team so they can be punished.

/map - Shows the current map playing and it’s authors.

/rot - Shows which maps will be playing next.

/server [name] - Teleports you to that server without needing to use the book.

/staff - Shows the current staff online, what ranks they have and what server they are on.



Navigating the Forums

The forums are a great place to keep up to date with information and update to the staff team, the server and new features. Let me walk you through some of the sub-topics found on the forums.

Avicus:

  • Announcements: Find important announcements here such as special promotions, updates and new, special features added to Avicus. Only staff will post threads in here.

  • Support: Here is an alternative to emailing support@avicus.net for staff member issues and personal issues with the senior staff team. This is different to Ask The Seniors as this is private whilst the other is public for all users to see.

  • Server Feedback: See feedback that other users leave as well as your own feedback and suggestions.

  • Guides & Support: This is where all guides and help threads are. If you need help with anything in more detail, this is the place to go to.

  • Ask The Seniors: Ask questions directed to senior moderators and Admin’s. Only the senior staff team will respond to your questions.

Community:

  • Trending Topics: Anything that the community find trendy and is repeated by the community can be found there. They won’t show on Recent Discussions but are still a great to learn a bit about other people depending on the topic.

  • Avicus Lounge: Any threads Avicus related that relate to Avicus and the server can be found here. You can discuss Avicus, updates and more.

  • Strategies & Tactics: Discuss various strategies and tactics used by other Avicus players. Want to learn how to be a better player? Something there will show you how.

  • Community Creations: This is a place where all Avicus players can create content that are strictly Avicus related. Channels and videos showcasing Avicus and it’s gamemodes can be found here. All non-Avicus content will be moved to off-topic.

  • Off Topic: All off topic threads will be found here. As long as threads aren’t spammy and follow the rules, they are allowed in off-topic.

  • Gaming Discussion: Somewhere you can all go to to talk about other games the community play.

  • Introduce Yourself: New to the community and the server? Introduce yourself and let us know a bit more about you as an individual. Also learn more about other players, old and new.

Map Development:

  • Map Making: Interested in making a map but need some help? Here you can collaborate with other map makers and help develop maps for the Avicus network, or gather opinions from map developers on improvements on your current map.

  • Map Releases: Finished a map and an xml? Release it here and gather opinions by other users and where or not it was accepted or denied by map developers. Who knows? Maybe your map may be the next map in the rotations.

Events:

  • Information: Find information on current and upcoming events in the making. Try and refrain from posting threads here unless they are an unofficial tournament or something related.

  • Discussion: Talk about events, predict the outcome and discuss the result of events and tournaments you can discuss with the rest of the community.

  • Looking For Team: Want to join a competitive team and compete in tournaments with your team? Make a post here and have team leaders invite you to join their team. These posts are not visible under Recent Discussions.

  • Looking For Members: Another way to join a team is to respond to team leaders seeking members for their team. These posts are not visible under Recent Discussions.

  • Looking For Scrimmage: Practice against other teams and prepare for the next event. These posts are not visible under Recent Discussions.

Policy:

  • Report A Player: Make an official report on other players breaking rules here. Staff will deal with the report and punish players if necessary. Abusing this sub-forum will result in punishments and forum bans.

  • Appeal An Infraction: Get punishments removed here. Got kicked/warned/banned unfairly? Get them removed and appealed here. Abusing this sub-forum will result in punishments and forum bans.

  • Teamspeak Appeals/Reports: Report those breaking the rules on our Teamspeak 3 server. You can also appeal punishments give on Teamspeak.

To view your profile on the forums, simply do https://avicus.net/[USERNAME] for example: https://avicus.net/_Cammy. This shows stats like total time spent on Avicus, kills, deaths, KD (kill/death ratio) and PvP KD plus most recent kills/deaths. You can also add some information about yourself under the “about” tab. To edit your profile and the information under your profile, go to the top right corner where you see your head and where you signed in, next to the “shop”, click on that and select “edit profile”, there you can add social media, edit the “about” section and your wallpaper.


See a small little “!” at the top of your screen in between the shop and your head? You have an alert! Alerts are messages that mean you have either had someone reply to your comment on a forum thread, added, removed, promoted or demoted you on a team, tagged you in a thread or tried to add/remove you as a friend. These can also be seen in-game by using /alerts.


Friends can be added/removed by going to a user’s profile on the forums and clicking “add friend,” This sends them an alert which they can accept or deny depending on whether they want to be your friend or not. Friends show up under your profile and you can see where they go as they move around the server and join/leave the server.

Now you can tag friends and other players in posts. Simple do {tag=[Name]} or when making a post, see the small person at the end of the row underneath where it asks for a title, click that and enter the players username and it will do it automatically. It, should look something like _Cammy which not only links you to their profile when you click on it but also alerts them.



Staff Ranks
Avicus has many different staff ranks that all players can earn. I'm going to to through every rank, what it does and how you can get it.

Administrator: These are the head of the server, they make the wonders of Avicus possible. They manage not only the community but also the staff team and oversee basically everything with an Avicus logo on it. These are selected by the senior staff team, but unless you are already a senior mod, you will have almost no chance of getting this rank.


Senior Moderator: These manage the server at a more in-depth level. They manage things like staff training, staff promotions/demotions and many more. They are selected by pre-existing senior moderators but you are going to need the moderator rank first.


Moderator: These moderate the server and make playing on Avicus the best as it can be. They punish those who break rules and answer questions asked by the community. Applications for this position come out every-so-often usually when there is a shortage of moderators, an interview usually soon follows.


Junior Moderator: This usually comes before moderator. After your interview and application or referral, you are given a junior moderator trial. You get all moderator commands, except /ban and /tempban. This usually goes for 3-4 weeks but varies depending on your performance.


Map Developer: These develop, manage and evaluate maps sent by the community. These are selected by pre-existing map developers.


Builder: These essentially build maps is is more a set up for map developer. These are selected by the map development team.


Official: These create, oversee and manage official tournaments. These are selected usually from the current referee's.


Referee: These help officials manage the tournaments by making sure things go smoothly and are cheat-free. Applications for this rank open every-so-often usually before a tournament.


Media: These stream tournaments. Applications for this rank open every-so-often usually before a tournament.


Developer: These basically develop the server. They are constantly adding new features, sorting out bugs and working on updates. These are selected by pre-existing developers.



I think that sums up just about the basics on How to Avicus? If you have anything that you should be added/edited/removed, let me know and I’ll get to it as soon as I can. This guide is expected to change as new stuff get’s added to the server. Any further questions, ask staff either in-game, teamspeak or the community slack, we are always happy to help.

Have a good one!

Cheers,

- Cammy

  • Strategies & Tactics: Discuss various strategies and tactics used by other Avicus players. Want to learn how to be a better player? Something there will show you how.

  • Community Creations: This is a place where all Avicus players can create content that are strictly Avicus related. Channels and videos showcasing Avicus and it’s gamemodes can be found here. All non-Avicus content will be moved to off-topic.

  • Off Topic: All off topic threads will be found here. As long as threads aren’t spammy and follow the rules, they are allowed in off-topic.

  • Gaming Discussion: Somewhere you can all go to to talk about other games the community play.

  • Introduce Yourself: New to the community and the server? Introduce yourself and let us know a bit more about you as an individual. Also learn more about other players, old and new.

Map Development:

  • Map Making: Interested in making a map but need some help? Here you can collaborate with other map makers and help develop maps for the Avicus network, or gather opinions from map developers on improvements on your current map.

  • Map Releases: Finished a map and an xml? Release it here and gather opinions by other users and where or not it was accepted or denied by map developers. Who knows? Maybe your map may be the next map in the rotations.

Events:

  • Information: Find information on current and upcoming events in the making. Try and refrain from posting threads here unless they are an unofficial tournament or something related.

  • Discussion: Talk about events, predict the outcome and discuss the result of events and tournaments you can discuss with the rest of the community.

  • Looking For Team: Want to join a competitive team and compete in tournaments with your team? Make a post here and have team leaders invite you to join their team. These posts are not visible under Recent Discussions.

  • Looking For Members: Another way to join a team is to respond to team leaders seeking members for their team. These posts are not visible under Recent Discussions.

  • Looking For Scrimmage: Practice against other teams and prepare for the next event. These posts are not visible under Recent Discussions.

Policy:

  • Report A Player: Make an official report on other players breaking rules here. Staff will deal with the report and punish players if necessary. Abusing this sub-forum will result in punishments and forum bans.

  • Appeal An Infraction: Get punishments removed here. Got kicked/warned/banned unfairly? Get them removed and appealed here. Abusing this sub-forum will result in punishments and forum bans.

  • Teamspeak Appeals/Reports: Report those breaking the rules on our Teamspeak 3 server. You can also appeal punishments give on Teamspeak.

To view your profile on the forums, simply do https://avicus.net/[USERNAME] for example: https://avicus.net/_Cammy. This shows stats like total time spent on Avicus, kills, deaths, KD (kill/death ratio) and PvP KD plus most recent kills/deaths. You can also add some information about yourself under the “about” tab. To edit your profile and the information under your profile, go to the top right corner where you see your head and where you signed in, next to the “shop”, click on that and select “edit profile”, there you can add social media, edit the “about” section and your wallpaper.


See a small little “!” at the top of your screen in between the shop and your head? You have an alert! Alerts are messages that mean you have either had someone reply to your comment on a forum thread, added, removed, promoted or demoted you on a team, tagged you in a thread or tried to add/remove you as a friend. These can also be seen in-game by using /alerts.


Friends can be added/removed by going to a user’s profile on the forums and clicking “add friend,” This sends them an alert which they can accept or deny depending on whether they want to be your friend or not. Friends show up under your profile and you can see where they go as they move around the server and join/leave the server.

Now you can tag friends and other players in posts. Simple do {tag=[Name]} or when making a post, see the small person at the end of the row underneath where it asks for a title, click that and enter the players username and it will do it automatically. It, should look something like _Cammy which not only links you to their profile when you click on it but also alerts them.



Staff Ranks
Avicus has many different staff ranks that all players can earn. I'm going to to through every rank, what it does and how you can get it.

Administrator: These are the head of the server, they make the wonders of Avicus possible. They manage not only the community but also the staff team and oversee basically everything with an Avicus logo on it. These are selected by the senior staff team, but unless you are already a senior mod, you will have almost no chance of getting this rank.


Senior Moderator: These manage the server at a more in-depth level. They manage things like staff training, staff promotions/demotions and many more. They are selected by pre-existing senior moderators but you are going to need the moderator rank first.


Moderator: These moderate the server and make playing on Avicus the best as it can be. They punish those who break rules and answer questions asked by the community. Applications for this position come out every-so-often usually when there is a shortage of moderators, an interview usually soon follows.


Junior Moderator: This usually comes before moderator. After your interview and application or referral, you are given a junior moderator trial. You get all moderator commands, except /ban and /tempban. This usually goes for 3-4 weeks but varies depending on your performance.


Map Developer: These develop, manage and evaluate maps sent by the community. These are selected by pre-existing map developers.


Builder: These essentially build maps is is more a set up for map developer. These are selected by the map development team.


Official: These create, oversee and manage official tournaments. These are selected usually from the current referee's.


Referee: These help officials manage the tournaments by making sure things go smoothly and are cheat-free. Applications for this rank open every-so-often usually before a tournament.


Media: These stream tournaments. Applications for this rank open every-so-often usually before a tournament.


Developer: These basically develop the server. They are constantly adding new features, sorting out bugs and working on updates. These are selected by pre-existing developers.



I think that sums up just about the basics on How to Avicus? If you have anything that you should be added/edited/removed, let me know and I’ll get to it as soon as I can. This guide is expected to change as new stuff get’s added to the server. Any further questions, ask staff either in-game, teamspeak or the community slack, we are always happy to help.

Have a good one!

Cheers,

- Cammy
